title: Free-response workshop: Reading the graph of a derivative
author: ab-workshop-author
directions: Work each question in 15 minutes, the exam's pace, writing answers in the space under each part. The Part A question requires a graphing calculator; Part B questions allow no calculator. Show supporting work and justify requested conclusions; write the setup for every calculator result, give calculator answers to three decimal places, and give exact answers in Part B. Then score your work with the answer key's rubric and record raw points. Raw points are practice evidence for AP® Calculus AB, not AP® scores.

figures.alt: Graph of y = f′(x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 5 on a grid with x marked every 1 and y every 0.5. The smooth curve starts at (0, −1), rises steeply, crosses the x-axis, reaches a single peak above the axis, then falls, crosses the x-axis again, and levels off just above y = −1 at x = 5.

Graph of y = f′(x) for −4 ≤ x ≤ 6 on a unit grid. A line segment rises from (−4, −2) to (−2, 2), and a second segment falls from (−2, 2) to (0, −2). From (0, −2) a quarter circle rises, starting vertically and curving to the right, until it meets the x-axis with a horizontal tangent at (2, 0). A last segment falls from (2, 0) to (6, −2).
Graph of r(t) for 0 ≤ t ≤ 12 on a unit grid. Line segments join the points (0, −2), (1, 0), (3, 4), (5, 4), (9, −4) and (12, 2) in order.

parts.directions: A graphing calculator is required. Show your work: write the integral, derivative, or equation you use before its value. Calculator answers are to three decimal places. Justify answers when a question asks you to.

items.prompt: The function f is differentiable on the closed interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 5, and f(2) = 1. The derivative of f is f′(x) = 3x·e^(−x^2/4) − 1, and the graph of f′ is shown in the figure.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find all values of x in the open interval 0 < x < 5 at which f has a relative minimum or a relative maximum. Classify each one, and justify your answers.

rubric.criterion: Solves f′(x) = 0 and finds x ≈ 0.343 and x ≈ 2.954, and no other values in 0 < x < 5.

Relative minimum at x ≈ 0.343 because f′ changes from negative to positive there; relative maximum at x ≈ 2.954 because f′ changes from positive to negative there. Both classifications, each with its sign change of f′, are needed.

parts.answer: f has a relative minimum at x ≈ 0.343 and a relative maximum at x ≈ 2.954.
steps: Solve 3x·e^(−x^2/4) − 1 = 0 on 0 < x < 5 with the calculator: x ≈ 0.343300734 and x ≈ 2.954213846. The graph of f′ shows no other zeros.
f′ changes from negative to positive at x ≈ 0.343, so f has a relative minimum there. f′ changes from positive to negative at x ≈ 2.954, so f has a relative maximum there.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of each point of inflection of the graph of f on the open interval 0 < x < 5. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Identifies x ≈ 1.414 (exactly √2), and no other value.
Justifies with f′ changing from increasing to decreasing at x ≈ 1.414, or with f″ changing from positive to negative there. "f″ = 0" alone does not earn this point.

steps: The graph of f changes concavity where f′ changes between increasing and decreasing, that is, where f″ changes sign.
f″(x) = 3e^(−x^2/4) − (3x^2/2)e^(−x^2/4) = 3e^(−x^2/4)(1 − x^2/2), which is zero on 0 < x < 5 only at x = √2 ≈ 1.414. A calculator's maximum feature on the graph of f′ gives the same x.
f″ > 0 on (0, √2) and f″ < 0 on (√2, 5): f′ increases and then decreases, so the graph of f has a point of inflection at x ≈ 1.414 and nowhere else in the interval.

parts.label: c

rubric.criterion: Writes f(5) = f(2) + ∫ from 2 to 5 of f′(x) dx, with the integrand or f′ named and the initial value 1.
f(5) ≈ 0.196, with the setup shown (accepts the exact value 6e^(−1) − 6e^(−25/4) − 2).

steps: f(5) = f(2) + ∫ from 2 to 5 of f′(x) dx = 1 + ∫ from 2 to 5 of (3x·e^(−x^2/4) − 1) dx.
The integral is ≈ −0.804306078, so f(5) ≈ 0.195693922, which rounds to 0.196.
An antiderivative of f′ is −6e^(−x^2/4) − x, which gives the same value exactly: f(5) = 1 + 6e^(−1) − 6e^(−25/4) − 3.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the absolute minimum value of f on the closed interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 5. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the candidates: the endpoints x = 0 and x = 5 and the critical points x ≈ 0.343 and x ≈ 2.954 (or uses the signs of f′ to limit the minimum to x = 0, x ≈ 0.343 and x = 5).
Evaluates f at the candidates with integral setups from f(2) = 1: f(0) ≈ −0.793 and f(0.343) ≈ −0.962 (with f(2.954) ≈ 1.576 and f(5) ≈ 0.196 as needed); accepts consistent use of f(5) from part (c).
Concludes that the absolute minimum value is about −0.962, at x ≈ 0.343, because it is the least candidate value.

parts.answer: The absolute minimum value of f on [0, 5] is f(0.343) ≈ −0.962.
steps: f is continuous on [0, 5], so its absolute minimum occurs at an endpoint or at a critical point: x = 0, x ≈ 0.343, x ≈ 2.954 or x = 5.
f(0.343) = 1 − ∫ from 0.343 to 2 of f′(x) dx ≈ −0.961820, using the stored zero 0.343300734 as the lower limit.

The least of the candidate values is about −0.962, so the absolute minimum value of f on [0, 5] is about −0.962, at x ≈ 0.343. The left endpoint comes close but is higher, because f falls a little between x = 0 and x ≈ 0.343.

parts.directions: No calculator is allowed. Show your work and give exact answers. Justify answers when a question asks you to; answers without supporting work may not earn credit.

items.prompt: The function f is differentiable on the closed interval −4 ≤ x ≤ 6, and f(0) = 4. The graph of its derivative f′, shown in the figure, consists of three line segments and a quarter of a circle. One segment joins (−4, −2) to (−2, 2), and a second joins (−2, 2) to (0, −2). The quarter circle has center (2, −2) and radius 2; it rises from (0, −2) to (2, 0), where its tangent line is horizontal. The third segment joins (2, 0) to (6, −2).

parts.label: a

rubric.criterion: f(−3) = f(0) − ∫ from −3 to 0 of f′(x) dx = 4 − 1 = 3, from the signed triangle areas 1, 1 and −1 on [−3, −2], [−2, −1] and [−1, 0].
f(6) = f(0) + ∫ from 0 to 6 of f′(x) dx = π − 4, using −(4 − π) for the region between the quarter circle and the x-axis on [0, 2] and −4 for the triangle on [2, 6].

steps: f(−3) = f(0) − ∫ from −3 to 0 of f′(x) dx. On [−3, −2] and [−2, −1] the graph forms triangles of area 1 above the axis; on [−1, 0] a triangle of area 1 below it. So ∫ from −3 to 0 of f′(x) dx = 1 + 1 − 1 = 1 and f(−3) = 4 − 1 = 3.

On [0, 2] the region between the quarter circle and the x-axis is the 2-by-2 square with corners (0, 0) and (2, −2) minus a quarter of a disk of radius 2, so its area is 4 − π, and it lies below the axis: ∫ from 0 to 2 of f′(x) dx = π − 4.
On [2, 6] the triangle has base 4 and height 2 below the axis: ∫ from 2 to 6 of f′(x) dx = −4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the absolute minimum value of f on the closed interval −4 ≤ x ≤ 6. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the candidates: the endpoints x = −4 and x = 6 and the critical points x = −3, x = −1 and x = 2, where f′(x) = 0 (or uses the signs of f′ to limit the minimum to x = −3 and x = 6).
Finds the candidate values f(−4) = 4, f(−3) = 3, f(−1) = 5, f(2) = π and f(6) = π − 4 (only f(−3) and f(6) are needed with a sign argument); accepts values carried consistently from part (a).
Concludes that the absolute minimum value is π − 4, at x = 6, supported by the comparison π − 4 < 0 < 3 (because π < 4).

parts.answer: The absolute minimum value of f on [−4, 6] is π − 4, at x = 6.
steps: Since π < 4, π − 4 < 0, which is less than every other candidate value. The absolute minimum value of f on [−4, 6] is π − 4, at x = 6.

x = 2 is a critical point but not a relative extremum: f′ ≤ 0 on both sides of it. The relative minimum at x = −3 is not the absolute minimum, because f keeps falling from x = −1 all the way to x = 6.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of each point of inflection of the graph of f on the open interval −4 < x < 6. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Identifies x = −2, x = 0 and x = 2, and no other values.
Justifies each with the change in direction of f′: from increasing to decreasing at x = −2 and x = 2, and from decreasing to increasing at x = 0 (or with the sign changes of f″).

steps: The concavity of f changes where f′ changes between increasing and decreasing.
f′ increases on (−4, −2), decreases on (−2, 0), increases on (0, 2) along the quarter circle, and decreases on (2, 6).
So the graph of f is concave up, then down, then up, then down, with points of inflection at x = −2, x = 0 and x = 2.

At x = 0 the slope of f′ does not exist (the quarter circle starts with a vertical tangent), and at x = 2 the value f′(2) = 0; neither fact matters by itself. What counts is that f′ changes direction at each of these points. The zeros x = −3 and x = −1 locate relative extrema of f, not points of inflection.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Let h be the function defined by h(x) = x·f(x). Find h′(4).

rubric.criterion: Uses the product rule, h′(x) = f(x) + x·f′(x), with f′(4) = −1 read from the graph.
Finds f(4) = π − 1 and h′(4) = π − 5; accepts a value of f(2) carried consistently from earlier work.

steps: By the product rule, h′(4) = f(4) + 4f′(4).
The segment from (2, 0) to (6, −2) has slope −1/2, so f′(4) = 0 + (−1/2)(2) = −1.
f(4) = f(2) + ∫ from 2 to 4 of f′(x) dx = π + (−1) = π − 1, using the triangle with base 2 and height 1 below the axis.

items.prompt: The temperature inside a greenhouse is T(t) degrees Celsius (°C), where t is the number of hours after 6 a.m., for 0 ≤ t ≤ 12. The temperature changes at the rate T′(t) = r(t) °C per hour. The graph of r, shown in the figure, consists of five line segments joining the points (0, −2), (1, 0), (3, 4), (5, 4), (9, −4) and (12, 2) in order. At time t = 0, the temperature inside the greenhouse is 14 °C.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find T(12). Find the average rate of change of the temperature over the interval 0 ≤ t ≤ 12, and give its units.

rubric.criterion: T(12) = 14 + ∫ from 0 to 12 of r(t) dt = 14 + 8 = 22 °C, with the integral shown.
Average rate of change = (T(12) − T(0))/12 = 2/3 °C per hour, with units; accepts consistent use of T(12).

parts.answer: T(12) = 22 °C. The average rate of change of the temperature over 0 ≤ t ≤ 12 is 2/3 °C per hour.
steps: Signed areas between the graph of r and the t-axis: −1 on [0, 1], 4 on [1, 3], 8 on [3, 5], 4 on [5, 7], −4 on [7, 9], −4 on [9, 11] and 1 on [11, 12]. They total 8.
Average rate of change = (T(12) − T(0))/(12 − 0) = 8/12 = 2/3 °C per hour.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: At what time t in the interval 0 ≤ t ≤ 12 is the temperature inside the greenhouse greatest? Find the greatest temperature. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Identifies t = 7 as the candidate where T′ = r changes from positive to negative (or lists t = 1, t = 7 and t = 11, where r = 0, with the endpoints as candidates).
T(7) = 14 + ∫ from 0 to 7 of r(t) dt = 29 °C.
Justifies the absolute maximum by comparing T(7) = 29 with T(0) = 14 and T(12) = 22 (and any other candidates used), or by the signs of r together with T(0) < T(7) and T(12) < T(7).

parts.answer: The temperature is greatest at t = 7 hours (1 p.m.), when it is 29 °C.
steps: T′(t) = r(t) is negative on (0, 1), positive on (1, 7), negative on (7, 11), and positive on (11, 12). The greatest temperature occurs at t = 0, t = 7 or t = 12.
T(0) = 14 and T(12) = 22 from part (a) are both less than 29, so the greatest temperature is 29 °C, at t = 7.
The rise on 11 < t < 12 is only 1 °C, far less than the 8 °C lost on 7 < t < 11, so the right endpoint cannot win.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find r′(8). Using correct units, explain the meaning of r′(8) in the context of the problem.

rubric.criterion: r′(8) = −2, the slope of the segment from (5, 4) to (9, −4).

Explains that at t = 8 hours the rate at which the temperature changes is decreasing by 2 °C per hour per hour (accepts °C/h^2). The explanation must be about the rate of change of the temperature, not the temperature itself.

parts.answer: r′(8) = −2 °C per hour per hour. At 8 hours after 6 a.m., the rate at which the greenhouse temperature changes is decreasing by 2 °C per hour each hour.
steps: On (5, 9) the graph of r is a segment with slope (−4 − 4)/(9 − 5) = −2, so r′(8) = −2.
r′ = T″ has the units of r divided by hours: °C per hour per hour.
At t = 8, r(8) = −2, so the temperature is already falling, and the rate of change keeps decreasing: the temperature falls faster each hour until t = 9.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For 0 < t < 12, on what open intervals is the temperature inside the greenhouse increasing at a decreasing rate? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the interval 5 < t < 7 only.
Reason: on 5 < t < 7, T′(t) = r(t) > 0, so the temperature increases, and r is decreasing, so the rate of increase decreases. Both conditions must be named.

parts.answer: 5 < t < 7, because there r(t) > 0 and r is decreasing.
steps: "Increasing at a decreasing rate" means T′ > 0 and T′ decreasing.
r > 0 on (1, 7). On (1, 3) r increases, on (3, 5) r is constant, and on (5, 7) r decreases.
On (11, 12), r > 0 but r is increasing. So the only such interval is 5 < t < 7.
